title: Kernel-probe benchmarking orchestration for attention variants and prefill/decode schedules
creator: Anya Patel
description:
Goal: Extend the benchmarking harness to systematically probe kernel selection and attention optimization interactions across representative workloads and prefill/decode scheduling policies, and to bake stable golden baselines + CI perf gates for kernel-level regressions.

Context: We see occasional tail-latency regressions tied to kernel routing choices under mixed workloads (short chat vs long prefill), and prototype sparse-attention kernels that reduce compute but change memory access patterns. Current bench suites cover end-to-end workloads but do not exercise fine-grained kernel switch points or prefill/decoder scheduling knobs at scale. This ticket designs an orchestration layer and workload catalog to: (1) surface kernel-specific regressions, (2) validate attention optimization variants (sparse/dense/rotary variants), and (3) add deterministic golden baselines and CI gates that run on PRs and nightly runs.

Scope:
- Add a kernel-probing mode in the harness that forces or samples specific kernel routing decisions (e.g., force int8 kernel, force fp16 fallback, prefer tiled-matmul vs fused-wg) and records per-kernel counters and latency distributions.
- Build attention-variant workloads: dense attention long-prefill (8k tokens), sparse attention mixed-turns (1k prefill + 64 token decode), rotary/ALiBi/linearized-attention variants with identical token sequences to compare validity.
- Extend prefill/decode scheduling scenarios: single large prefill followed by burst decode, many short prefill batches, KV-cache-warmup vs cold-start, and mixed-tenant batching.
- Produce golden baselines: canonical seeds, deterministic RNG/run order, hardware and compiler config tags, and hashed artifact of param sizes and kernel mapping.
- CI perf gates: implement automated checks for median and tail regressions (p50, p95, p99) against golden baselines; allow configurable sensitivity by project and model family.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Risks & trade-offs: Forcing kernels reduces representativeness of production routing—we will maintain both forced-probe runs and traffic-weighted simulated runs to balance fidelity. Attention-variant synthetic workloads may overfit optimizations; we will ensure real customer trace-derived corpus is included. Harness runtime cost will increase: gate cadence and selective sampling will mitigate infra costs.

Artifacts to produce: orchestration config (yaml), workload manifests (jsonl), runner scripts for kernel-probe, updated telemetry schema for per-kernel counters, CI job definitions (circle/gha), and a short runbook for investigating failures.
acceptance_criteria: Kernel-probe mode implemented and selectable via harness CLI/config
Workload catalog includes at least 6 attention variants and 5 prefill/decode schedules (listed in artifact)
Golden baseline snapshots committed for two representative models (medium and long-context), including a reproducible seed and environment hash
CI perf gate job added to PR pipeline that runs a fast subset and nightly full run that computes p50/p95/p99 deltas vs golden baseline
Regression alerting documented with triage playbook and automated ticket template when regression exceeds threshold
progress_updates: 2025-11-04 - Spike: benchmarked forcing int8 vs fp16 on small transformer (3B) across 3 hardware targets; discovered a 12% p95 increase on A100 for sparse kernel due to memory thrash when batch=1

2025-11-07 - Design review with runtime team: decided to implement a sampling policy that forces kernels for 5% of requests in simulated runs and 100% for dedicated probe runs; agreed on telemetry tags 'kernel_probe=true' and 'probe_variant'
2025-11-11 - First PR: added kernel-probe CLI flag and per-kernel latency logging (PR #faked/4321); waiting review from infra and telemetry owners

2025-11-15 - Added three attention workloads (dense_long_prefill, sparse_mixed_short, rotary_chat_sim) and canonical seeds. Ran golden baseline for medium model and recorded artifacts in GCS at gs://redwood-bench/gold/ENG-90587/medium/2025-11-15

2025-11-18 - CI plan drafted: fast gate on PRs to run 3 short probes (smoke) and nightly job to run full 12-scenario suite. Gate thresholds: alert if p95 increases >6% or p50 increases >10% relative to baseline for a given kernel mapping
next_steps: Finish PR feedback, add telemetry schema changes to runtime-telemetry repo, wire CI job with artifact storage and thresholding logic, run end-to-end nightly baseline for long-context model, and schedule runway demo with PM and Applied ML team. After initial run, evaluate false-positive rate of gates and tune sampling fraction.
notes: Be conservative with forced-kernel sampling in shared infra to avoid perturbing production tenants. Keep an immutable record of environment hashes so we can attribute regressions to compiler/kernel changes vs harness noise. Coordinate with Model-Onboarding to ensure model config parity when comparing baselines.
